subject: DPA redlines (data transfers & subprocessors) — signature risk; need exec OK
messages:

To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finservco.com>

Subject: FinServCo DPA redlines and subprocessor list

Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood. Legal asked me to send our redlines to the DPA and the current subprocessor inventory so you can route internally. Attached: FinServCo_DPA_redline_v2.docx and FinServCo_Subprocessor_List.xlsx.

High level points from our side:
- Data transfer clause: we need clarity on adequacy/Standard Contractual Clauses and whether Redwood will be the exporter/controller for any EU-sourced data.
- Subprocessors: we flag two infra partners (EdgeCloudCo, StorageBox). We need confirmation of guarantees and a timely notification process for new subprocessors.
- Security exception: we asked for a carve-out for audit evidence related to SOC2 reports and encryption key custody.

We have a tight procurement window — our commercial team is working toward signature by 8/14 to align with quarter close. Can you confirm timeline for legal review and whether Redwood needs a formal exception/board sign-off for any of the items above?

Thanks,
Sara Ross
General Counsel
FinServCo

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServCo DPA redlines and subprocessor list

Team — I reviewed FinServCo's v2 redline. Summary of painful points and our recommended actions: 

1) Data transfers / SCCs
- They are asking for explicit exporter/controller text. For our hosted product we typically act as processor and adopt SCCs. Accepting controller wording increases our exposure.
- Recommended: propose processor role + SCCs + an additional recital confirming we will cooperate on transfer mechanisms.

2) Key custody / KMS requirement
- Redline asks for customer-managed keys (BYOK) for certain categories. We can support HSM-backed keys in Dedicated/Private, but not the hosted multi-tenant SKU without engineering work.
- Recommended: offer conditional KMS commitments for Dedicated/Private; propose an implementation timeline and a separate commercial addendum.

3) Subprocessor notice & liability cap
- They want 30 days' notice and unlimited liability for subprocessor breaches. We need to keep liability caps and retain a notification window but can offer 30 days for major infra changes.
- Recommended: accept 30-day notice for new subprocessors; push for liability cap tied to fees.

4) Audit rights
- They requested full onsite audits. We prefer SOC2 reports + virtual reviews and a redacted architecture doc.

Risk/approval ask: the KMS and controller designation are the two items that may require a formal exception if we concede. Priyom — can you provide an initial risk position and whether security is comfortable with the conditional commitments above? If not, we need to escalate to VP Legal/Revenue for exception approval.

I’ll prepare a tracked-changes response to send to FinServCo if we get greenlight on the KMS/ controller language approach.

—Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServCo DPA redlines and subprocessor list

Karthik — thanks for the summary. Quick risk position from Security: 

- Controller designation: not acceptable for hosted; can consider controller-like assurances (SCCs + processing terms) but only if product-level mitigations (data localization + access controls) are documented. No exception required if we keep processor role.
- KMS: we can support HSM/BYOK in Dedicated/Private. For hosted, offering BYOK would need a discrete engineering project and a timeline — we should not promise immediate support.
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is reasonable for major infra providers; we should keep automated registry updates and a contractual notification clause.

Business tradeoff: FinServCo is asking to sign by 8/14. If we push back on BYOK for hosted, we risk losing the deal in the near term. If Sales wants to accelerate, we should propose an interim mitigant (enhanced contract commitments + SOC2 evidence) and a product roadmap item for BYOK.

Decision needed: do we allow Sales to offer a conditional exception for BYOK (hosted) with a product commit timeline and a price uplift, or hold firm and request they move to Dedicated? Lauren / Jordan — advise.

—Priyom
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServCo DPA redlines and subprocessor list

Team — procurement just told me FinServCo will pause the signature process if we don’t provide a BYOK path for hosted within the next 10 business days. Sales is reporting a $1.2M ARR new logo and the customer cannot move to Dedicated this quarter due to budget.

Proposal to expedite:
- Offer an interim contract amendment: commit to BYOK feasibility study and a concrete delivery milestone (e.g., prototype in 60 days, GA in 120 days) and an explicit price uplift for hosted BYOK.
- Provide immediate compensating controls: updated SOC2 report, formalized subprocessor notification SLA, and redacted architecture/KMS control docs.
- Require exec-level sign-off (Revenue/Legal/Security) on the exception and the product timeline.

Karthik/Prioym/Jordan — please confirm you can sign off on the language below by EOD so I can respond to Sara and prevent FinServCo from pausing. I’ll prepare the DocuSign envelope as soon as we have approvals: https://app.docusign.com/finish?env=na1&token=ABC123DEF

—Lauren
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
